title: India-UAE Festive Flights From Dh945 as Diwali Travel Demand Picks Up
excerpt: UAE–India return fares start at Dh945 for the Oct 19–Nov 9 window, but travel agents expect prices to climb from mid-October as Dussehra and Diwali bookings gather pace.
body:
• Return fares from the UAE to India start at Dh945 (Dubai/Sharjah to Bengaluru) for travel between October 19 and November 9: Dubai–Mumbai from Dh1,072, Dubai–Kochi Dh1,042, Dubai–Hyderabad Dh1,017, Dubai–New Delhi Dh1,439.
  • Dussehra is October 20 and Diwali is November 8, 2026; travel agents say fares are still affordable now but expect prices to rise from mid-October as bookings gather pace.
  • Air India expects passenger numbers to strengthen further in October and November; its winter schedule runs 272 India–UAE flights per week from October 26.
  • Book now — don't bank on last-minute deals. Routes with fewer direct flights (Dubai–Varanasi ~Dh2,303, Dubai–Jaipur ~Dh1,426) are already pricier and will tighten first.

Fares for festive-season travel between India and the UAE are still affordable — but the window is closing. Return fares for the October 19 to November 9 travel period start at Dh945 from Dubai to Bengaluru, according to Gulf News, with travel agents reporting that prices will begin rising from mid-October as Dussehra (October 20) and Diwali (November 8, 2026) demand builds.

The fare picture

""Fares remained relatively affordable for now, but last-minute bookings were likely to increase and ticket prices could begin rising from mid-October," she said."

The cheapest returns in the surveyed window: Dubai–Bengaluru from Dh945 and Sharjah–Bengaluru from Dh945, with Sharjah's affordable Air Arabia options helping keep the corridor competitive. Other Dubai departures: Mumbai from Dh1,072, Hyderabad from Dh1,017, Kochi from Dh1,042, New Delhi from Dh1,439, Chennai (Sharjah) from Dh1,205, and Tiruchirapalli (Sharjah) around Dh1,370. Tier-2 cities with fewer direct flights are markedly pricier — Dubai–Jaipur around Dh1,426 and Dubai–Varanasi near Dh2,303 — and those are the routes where seats will fill first.

Demand is holding

Sapna Aidasani, marketing director at Dubai's Pluto Travels, told Gulf News that demand among Indian expatriates remains strong, with enquiries for Dussehra and Diwali group travel beginning to increase — and interest in Christmas and New Year travel already strong. "Fares remained relatively affordable for now, but last-minute bookings were likely to increase and ticket prices could begin rising from mid-October," she said. Gujarat and Mumbai markets are expected to drive much of the demand, with the post-Diwali wedding season adding more India-bound travel.

PP Singh, Air India's regional manager for the Gulf, Middle East and Africa, said bookings are healthy with some last-minute activity, and expects passenger numbers to strengthen further in October and November. Air India's winter schedule — running October 26 through end of March — will operate a combined 272 flights per week between India and the UAE with Air India Express (54 on Air India itself), and the airline is back to 100% of its permitted capacity under the India–UAE bilateral agreement following disruptions from the US–Iran war earlier this year.

Diaspora angle: what to do now

For the 3.5-million-strong Indian diaspora in the UAE, the math is simple: fares under Dh1,500 are still available across the October 19–November 9 window, but they will not last. Cleartrip data corroborates the picture — bookings for Dussehra and Diwali are picking up sharply even as airfares sit roughly 20% higher than a year ago, driven partly by jet fuel costs that have roughly doubled since the February 2026 Middle East war and the Strait of Hormuz closure. The reverse direction (India→UAE) is less affected, since UAE schools and universities don't observe Diwali holidays. Book the outbound now; don't wait for a sale that isn't coming.

What's next

Mehar Sawlani, director of sales at Richmond Gulf Tourism, noted that India→UAE demand is healthy as Dubai enters peak tourism season, though demand has "yet to return to levels recorded before the war." As the October 26 winter schedule kicks in with full bilateral capacity, the binding constraint this festive season will be seats on tier-2 routes — exactly the ones already priced at a premium.
